newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: INTERVIEW-Thai woes should not deter Asian nations.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Thai woes should not deter Asian nations.

text.p: Thailand's economic crisis should not discourage other Asian countries from moving ahead with market liberalisation, Pacific Basin Economic Council (PBEC) chairman Gary Tooker said on Wednesday.

"Each economy should recognise and come to grips with what is appropriate for them. But I think there are plenty of examples that privatisation and reduction of barriers have led to a better quality of life and enhanced business conditions in all economies," Tooker told Reuters.
"So we are encouraging leaders to move forward at a pace that is appropriate for them, but they have to continue to move in that direction," he added.
Thailand's economic growth is projected to slow drastically this year, hit by a slowdown in exports, poor company earnings and problems in the sluggish property market.
These problems have been attended by a plummeting stock market and speculative attacks on the Thai baht that have prompted fears the currency would be devalued.

The PBEC, comprising 1,200 corporations in 20 economies in the region, is meeting in Manila where it has urged the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation forum (APEC) to push harder for market reforms among its members.

Bangkok Bank Plc president Chartsiri Sophonpanich earlier warned Asian economies against plunging into market liberalisation at a breakneck speed as it would bring only "disappointment and misery" in the future.
Tooker said businessmen were content with the pace Asian governments are opening up their economies.
"I think the moves have been very positive. The privatisation and dropping of trade barriers are moves in the right direction," added Tooker, who is also chairman of technology giant Motorola Inc.
